root_cause: The MicroModal library's getFocusableNodes() method only filters out elements with the 'hidden' attribute or inside a '[hidden]' ancestor, but does not exclude elements hidden via CSS display:none. The 'Try again' button (#retry) inside .optional-retry {display:none} remains in the focusable nodes array, making it the last focusable element. When Shift+Tab is pressed from the first element (#email), focus attempts to move to #retry (index 3), but since it's display:none, focus stays on #email instead of wrapping to #close (index 2).
repair_strategy: Modify getFocusableNodes() in micromodal.js to additionally filter out elements that have zero rendered dimensions (width/height 0), which excludes CSS display:none elements like #retry while preserving all visibly rendered dialog controls.
expected_accessibility_effect: Restores correct bidirectional Tab/Shift+Tab focus cycling through only visibly rendered dialog controls (#email → #confirm → #close → #email), preserving the fixed Cancel button in the tab order and preventing focus from escaping the modal.
functional_risks: Elements intentionally sized to 0x0 but focusable (rare) would be excluded
Computed layout may briefly report 0 during animations; however dialog is static when focus trapping runs
verification_requirements: Shift+Tab from #email moves focus to #close (step 3 passes)
Tab from #close moves focus to #email (step 6 passes)
Enter on #confirm closes dialog, shows receipt, returns focus to #open (step 9 passes)
All functional invariants (receipt text, data attributes, visibility) hold
